text.p: Nigeria's military government has sacked more than 2,000 customs officers, many of them for corrupt practices, the national news agency reported on Sunday.
The News Agency of Nigeria quoted Brigadier-General Samuel Ango, head of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), as saying at the weekend that the figure was likely to increase.
About 1,000 of the officers were sacked as a result of corrupt practices, Ango said, adding: "We believe there is no need to wash our dirty linens outside, but we will certainly wash them."
Ango said eight customs officers implicated in the U.S. television network station, Columbia Broadcasting Service (CBS), documentary in 1994 had been disciplined.

Some of the eight were secretly filmed as they demanded and received bribes at the Lagos airport from the CBS crew that visited Nigeria in 1994 to produce a documentary film on fraud practices. It was later broadcast in the Unietd States.
In 1995, the military government tightened collection of customs dues at the ports after the Federal Finance Ministry said there was laxity and corruption in the customs service.
It also eliminated the chaotic procedures and delays associated with clearance of goods at the ports, for which it has introduced the use of computers.
The reforms shot earnings at the ports to 55 billion naira ($688 million) in 1996 from 39 billion naira in 1995, according to Finance Minister Anthony Ani.
